quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Subject: Changes to client reporting from January. Dear team, following feedback from several clients, we will replace the monthly PDF report with an online dashboard from January. The dashboard shows campaign results in real time, and clients will be able to filter by date, region and channel. This means account managers will no longer spend the first week of each month assembling figures; instead, that time should be used to advise clients on what the numbers mean. Some clients may prefer a summary, so a short written note will still be sent each quarter. Training sessions will run on 9 and 10 December, and attendance is compulsory for anyone managing an account. Please note that historical data before 2023 will not be transferred, so keep your own copies of older reports. Questions should be sent to Rhea Malik, who is coordinating the change. Any concerns from clients about the change should be passed to your regional lead before the end of this month.
quests.question: What are account managers expected to do with the time saved?
options: Attend training sessions in December
Advise clients about what the results mean
Transfer historical data to the dashboard
Prepare a quarterly written note
quests.correctAnswer: Advise clients about what the results mean
quests.hint: The freed time is described after a linking word meaning "in place of".
quests.explanation: The email says the time formerly spent assembling reports should be used for advising clients. The quarterly note and training are separate tasks.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Public notice: closure of Harbour Bridge for maintenance. The council will close Harbour Bridge to all vehicles from 10 p.m. on Friday 12 September until 5 a.m. on Monday 15 September so that contractors can replace expansion joints. Pedestrians and cyclists may use the bridge throughout, although a narrow lane will be separated by barriers and speeds should be kept low. Buses on routes 4 and 11 will be diverted via the ring road, adding around fifteen minutes to journeys; a free shuttle will connect Quay Street and the station every twenty minutes. Emergency vehicles will be given priority access and will have a dedicated route via Mill Lane. Residents in the affected streets are asked to avoid parking outside their homes on Friday night, since large machinery will need room to manoeuvre. Businesses may apply for a small compensation payment before 30 September. Please note that the pedestrian lane is not suitable for large groups, and cyclists are asked to dismount on the central section.
quests.question: Why are residents asked not to park outside their homes on Friday night?
options: Large machinery will need space to move
Emergency vehicles use those streets as a route
The pavement will be closed for cyclists
The shuttle will stop there
quests.correctAnswer: Large machinery will need space to move
quests.hint: The request is followed by "since" and a reason.
quests.explanation: Heavy machinery needs room to manoeuvre. The emergency route runs via Mill Lane, not through these streets.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: The Solari 500 portable solar charger folds into a case the size of a paperback and is designed for hikers and travellers. Its four panels deliver up to 20 watts in direct sunlight, enough to charge a smartphone in about two hours, though the figure falls sharply under cloud. An internal battery stores energy for use at night, but it must itself be charged fully before first use, which takes around eight hours from a wall socket. Two USB ports allow two devices to charge together, at the cost of slower charging for each. The charger is water-resistant but not waterproof, and should not be left in a puddle. It weighs 480 grams and comes with a carabiner for attaching to a backpack. The manufacturer offers a twelve-month guarantee against faults, but not against damage from misuse. Spare panels and replacement cables can be ordered from the website, and delivery is free for orders over thirty dollars.
quests.question: What is a disadvantage of charging two devices simultaneously?
options: Each device charges more slowly
The internal battery stops working
The panels overheat in sunlight
The charger cannot be attached to a backpack
quests.correctAnswer: Each device charges more slowly
quests.hint: Look for the phrase that signals a trade-off.
quests.explanation: Two ports work at once but with slower charging per device. Battery use at night and the carabiner are unrelated.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Report summary: Student wellbeing survey. Of the 1,120 students who responded, 68 percent said they felt supported by their teachers, a rise of six points since last year. However, 41 percent reported feeling anxious about exams, and 27 percent said they regularly slept fewer than six hours on school nights. The most common reason for lost sleep was the use of phones late at night, followed by homework. Students who took part in sport or clubs reported higher wellbeing than those who did not, although the report cautions that the direction of the relationship is unclear: happier students may simply be more likely to join activities. The school will pilot a "digital sunset" policy, encouraging pupils to switch off devices an hour before bedtime, and will review homework loads in the spring. A summary of the findings will be shared with parents at the next open evening, and pupils will be invited to suggest improvements.
quests.question: What does the report say about students who join clubs?
options: They feel less supported by teachers than other students
They receive less homework because of their activities
They sleep fewer hours than students who do not join
They report higher wellbeing, but the reason for this is uncertain
quests.correctAnswer: They report higher wellbeing, but the reason for this is uncertain
quests.hint: A cautious verb tells you the writers do not claim a cause.
quests.explanation: The report links activities to wellbeing but says happier students may be more likely to join, so causation is unclear.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: For decades, a lecture was a professor speaking and students writing. Many universities are now experimenting with alternatives because studies show that active learning improves results. In an "active" session, students spend part of the time solving problems in small groups, voting on answers with their phones or explaining an idea to a neighbour. The lecturer walks around the room, listening for misunderstandings. A large analysis of more than two hundred studies found that failure rates fell by about a third in courses that used these methods. Not all students welcome the change: some say they prefer to listen quietly and complain that group work is uncomfortable. Yet teachers point out that the discomfort is often a sign that learning is happening, since effort, not passive listening, builds understanding. Some departments have already redesigned their timetables so that a full third of every session is devoted to discussion and problem solving.
quests.question: What is the teachers' response to students who dislike group work?
options: Students should listen quietly instead of joining groups
Discomfort often shows that real learning is taking place
Failure rates depend mainly on lecturers' salaries
Phones should be banned from all lectures
quests.correctAnswer: Discomfort often shows that real learning is taking place
quests.hint: A word of contrast introduces the teachers' view.
quests.explanation: Teachers argue that effort, not passive listening, builds understanding, so some discomfort is expected. Phones are used to vote, not banned.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: When ordering by weight, remember that carriers charge for the greater of actual and volumetric weight. Volumetric weight is calculated by multiplying the parcel's length, width and height in centimetres and dividing by 5,000. A pillow packed in a large box may weigh only one kilogram but be charged as eight, since it occupies a great deal of space in the vehicle. To save money, choose the smallest box in which the item fits with protection, and avoid oversized packaging. Fragile goods should be surrounded by at least three centimetres of cushioning. International shipments also require a customs form listing the contents and value; incorrect descriptions can delay delivery or lead to extra charges. Insurance covers loss or damage up to the declared value, but claims must be made within fourteen days. Customers should photograph the parcel before sealing it, as this makes any later claim simpler to process.
quests.question: Why might a lightweight pillow be charged as eight kilograms?
options: The customs form is incomplete
The pillow is fragile and needs insurance
The carrier uses a different scale
The parcel is large in relation to its weight
quests.correctAnswer: The parcel is large in relation to its weight
quests.hint: Follow the two weights the carrier compares and see which one wins for a big box.
quests.explanation: Volumetric weight depends on box size, so a large box holding a light item is charged for the space it takes up.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Dear residents, we are writing about the new bin collection arrangements from 1 October. General waste will now be collected every three weeks instead of fortnightly, while food waste will continue weekly. The council has taken this decision because, in trials, households recycled more and produced less rubbish when the interval was longer. Recycling will still be collected fortnightly, and you can order a larger blue bin free of charge if you find yours too small. Households with babies in nappies or people with medical conditions producing extra waste can apply for an additional collection; please use the form on our website, attaching a letter from a doctor or health visitor. Residents in flats with communal bins will see no change. A calendar showing your collection dates will be delivered by 15 September. Residents who are unsure which bin to use for a particular item can consult the online guide or call the recycling helpline.
quests.question: Who can apply for an additional collection?
options: Families with babies in nappies and people with medical waste needs
Anyone who simply wants a weekly general waste collection
All households that have a blue recycling bin in the district
Residents of flats that share communal bins
quests.correctAnswer: Families with babies in nappies and people with medical waste needs
quests.hint: One sentence names the groups with special circumstances.
quests.explanation: Babies' nappies and medical conditions qualify, with a supporting letter. Flats with communal bins are unaffected by the changes.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: Travellers arriving at Kestrel International Airport can reach the city centre in three ways. The airport express train takes twenty minutes and runs every ten minutes from 5 a.m. to midnight; a single ticket costs $14, or $22 return valid for the day. The bus is slower, taking about fifty minutes, but costs only $5 and runs through the night, with a reduced service after 1 a.m. Taxis are available outside arrivals and cost about $45, although traffic at peak times can double the journey time. Passengers with heavy luggage might prefer the train, which has designated luggage racks. Tickets for both train and bus can be bought at machines in the terminal or via the airport app, which also offers a five percent discount on return tickets. Children under five travel free on both services, and the airport app shows live departure times for each option.
quests.question: Which option would suit a passenger arriving at 2 a.m. on a small budget?
options: The airport app
The airport express train
The bus
A taxi
quests.correctAnswer: The bus
quests.hint: Combine the arrival time with the price constraint, then check which option operates.
quests.explanation: The train stops at midnight and taxis are expensive, while the bus runs through the night for $5.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor but support about a quarter of all marine species. They grow slowly, as tiny animals called polyps build limestone skeletons, and they depend on algae that live inside the polyps and provide most of their food. When the water becomes too warm, the polyps expel the algae, and the coral turns white, a process known as bleaching. Bleached coral is not dead, and it can recover if temperatures fall quickly. However, repeated events, as happened across several reefs in the last decade, leave little time for regrowth. Researchers are testing ways to help, such as breeding heat-tolerant coral, but they emphasise that these are only supplements to reducing carbon emissions. In the most severe cases, reefs have lost more than half of their live coral within a single year, according to survey teams.
quests.question: What does bleaching mean in this passage?
options: Coral loses its algae because of warm water
Coral is killed by pollution
Polyps build faster limestone skeletons
Algae grow too rapidly on the coral
quests.correctAnswer: Coral loses its algae because of warm water
quests.hint: Find the sentence that defines the term, using "known as".
quests.explanation: When water is too warm, polyps expel the algae, turning white. The coral is not dead at that stage.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: The new parental leave policy takes effect on 1 April. Employees who have completed six months of service are entitled to twenty weeks of paid leave, which can be taken by either parent, and up to an additional twelve weeks unpaid. Leave may be taken in one block or divided into two periods, provided the second begins within twelve months of the birth or adoption. Employees should inform their manager at least eight weeks in advance, although exceptions will be made for early births. During leave, benefits such as health insurance continue unchanged. On return, employees may request a phased schedule of three or four days a week for up to three months, with pay adjusted accordingly. HR will hold information sessions on 12 and 19 March, and a confidential helpline is available for questions. Employees who become foster parents are entitled to the same leave, and part-time staff receive it in proportion to their hours.
quests.question: What condition applies if leave is divided into two periods?
options: The second period must begin within a year of the birth or adoption
Managers must approve each period in writing at least a month before
The second period must be unpaid, whatever the case
Both periods must be taken by the same parent of the child
quests.correctAnswer: The second period must begin within a year of the birth or adoption
quests.hint: A conditional word introduces the requirement on the split.
quests.explanation: Splitting is allowed provided the second period starts within twelve months. Either parent may take leave, so option one is wrong.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: A recent article claimed that people who drink coffee live longer, and it was shared widely. A closer look shows why such headlines deserve caution. The study followed half a million people for ten years and found that those who drank two to three cups a day were about ten percent less likely to die in that period. But coffee drinkers may differ from others in many ways, such as income, diet or exercise, and the researchers could not fully account for these. The study also relied on people reporting their own habits, which is not always reliable. In addition, the researchers grouped all forms of coffee together, including sweetened drinks, which makes the results harder to interpret. Its authors themselves say only that coffee is "not harmful" for most adults. The headline, in other words, said more than the evidence did.
quests.question: What is the writer's criticism of the coffee headline?
options: The study was too small to be useful
Coffee shortens life for most people who drink it
The headline overstated what the study actually showed
The researchers deliberately lied about their results
quests.correctAnswer: The headline overstated what the study actually showed
quests.hint: The final sentence sums up the writer's judgement of the headline.
quests.explanation: The authors claim only that coffee is not harmful, whereas the headline suggested longer life, so it went beyond the evidence.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: The Elmwood Library is trialling a "library of things" alongside its books. Members can borrow items such as drills, sewing machines, camping tents and board games for up to two weeks, free of charge. The scheme began after a survey showed that many residents bought tools they used only once. Items are kept in a room at the back and loaned through the normal desk. Borrowers must be over eighteen and are asked to sign a short form accepting responsibility for damage caused by misuse, though normal wear and tear is not charged. Popular items, such as the carpet cleaner, are booked weeks ahead, so the library is considering buying more. A "repair cafe" on the first Saturday of each month teaches people to mend small items instead of throwing them away. The library also hopes to add a small collection of musical instruments, provided that a local donor can be found to cover the cost.
quests.question: What is the reason for starting the scheme?
options: Residents were buying tools they rarely used
Volunteers wanted to sell items to raise money
Books were becoming less popular among residents
The library had too much empty space
quests.correctAnswer: Residents were buying tools they rarely used
quests.hint: The origin of the project is in the sentence containing the word "began".
quests.explanation: A survey found many residents bought tools for one-off use, which prompted the loan scheme. Popularity of some items came later.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Rosa's grandfather worked on the railway for forty years, and when he died she found in his shed a wooden box of tools so worn that the handles had taken the shape of his hands. She had never been interested in carpentry, but she took them home, and one evening she tried to plane a piece of pine. It went badly. Her first joints were crooked, and the wood split twice. Yet she noticed how calm she felt while concentrating on something small and physical, after a day spent in front of a screen. Within a year, she had built a bookcase, and within two she was teaching a Saturday class at the community workshop. She still uses her grandfather's tools, and when students admire them, she says that the handles are the best teachers she has ever had.
quests.question: What does Rosa mean when she says the handles are her best teachers?
options: The handles are decorated with instructions
Her grandfather taught her to plane wood
The worn shape shows her how to hold and use the tools
The tools are more expensive than modern ones
quests.correctAnswer: The worn shape shows her how to hold and use the tools
quests.hint: Ask what the worn shape of the handles could teach a beginner.
quests.explanation: The handles have been shaped by years of use, so they guide her grip. Her grandfather is described as a railway worker, not as her teacher.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Reduce your energy bills this winter with five simple steps. First, lower your thermostat by one degree; most people do not notice the difference, but it can cut heating costs by around ten percent. Second, close curtains at dusk to keep heat in, and open them during the day to let sunshine warm the room. Third, draught-proof windows and doors, which is inexpensive and can save the equivalent of a month's heating over the season. Fourth, bleed radiators if they are cold at the top, since trapped air stops them heating properly. Finally, wash clothes at thirty degrees and avoid using the tumble dryer where possible. Households on low incomes may qualify for free insulation; check the eligibility guide on our website or call our advice line. Simple changes made together in one week can reduce a typical household's heating bill by a noticeable margin, so it is worth trying them all.
quests.question: According to the text, why should radiators be bled?
options: They are cold at the bottom instead of the top
They use more electricity than newer radiators
The curtains are blocking the heat from the room
Trapped air prevents them from heating properly
quests.correctAnswer: Trapped air prevents them from heating properly
quests.hint: The reason follows "since" in the fourth step.
quests.explanation: Air trapped inside stops the radiator from heating fully, so bleeding it restores performance. The problem is described as coldness at the top.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: A new study of commuting suggests that shorter journeys are not always happier ones. Researchers interviewed 5,000 workers about their daily travel and found that those who walked or cycled reported greater satisfaction than drivers, even when the journey was longer. The explanation seems to lie in control and activity: walkers and cyclists are less affected by traffic and arrive feeling more awake. Train passengers reported mixed feelings, depending on whether they could get a seat and use the time to read or relax. The unhappiest group consisted of people who drove more than an hour in heavy traffic. The authors note that people who choose active travel may differ in other ways, but they believe that employers who provide showers and secure bike storage could increase satisfaction at low cost. Several companies have responded by allowing staff to start later or finish earlier, so that they can travel outside the rush hour.
quests.question: What can be concluded about walkers and cyclists?
options: They have shorter journeys than everyone else
They are often happier than drivers, even on longer journeys
They arrive later at work than drivers
They dislike traffic more than train passengers do
quests.correctAnswer: They are often happier than drivers, even on longer journeys
quests.hint: Compare the groups in the second sentence, ignoring the length of the journey.
quests.explanation: The study found that active commuters reported more satisfaction than drivers even when their trips were longer.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Following the fire alarm test last Thursday, we would like to remind all staff of the evacuation procedure. When the alarm sounds, stop what you are doing, leave the building by the nearest exit and go to the assembly point in the east car park. Do not use the lifts. Fire wardens, identified by orange vests, will check each floor and are responsible for making sure no one is left behind. Visitors should be accompanied by the person they are meeting. Once outside, please stay with your team and wait for the roll call; nobody may re-enter the building until the fire service gives permission. Staff who need assistance to leave, for example due to mobility problems, should contact facilities so that a personal evacuation plan can be drawn up. Anyone who discovers a fire should raise the alarm by breaking the nearest glass panel and then leave immediately.
quests.question: Who is responsible for ensuring that nobody is left on a floor?
options: Each employee's own line manager
The fire wardens in orange vests
The fire service when it arrives
The hosts of visitors in the building
quests.correctAnswer: The fire wardens in orange vests
quests.hint: The role is described together with a visual identifier.
quests.explanation: Fire wardens check floors, and they are identified by orange vests. Hosts look after visitors only.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Choosing where to spend a limited holiday budget often comes down to a trade-off. A city break offers museums, restaurants and short travel times, but hotel prices are high and the days can be exhausting. A beach holiday is cheaper per day and requires less planning, though the cost of flights in July and August can offset the savings. A walking holiday in the mountains is inexpensive once you arrive, since huts and campsites cost little, but you need equipment and reasonable fitness. Whichever you choose, travelling outside school holidays usually reduces prices by a quarter or more. The most important advice is to decide in advance what you want to get from the trip, whether rest, culture or challenge, rather than being led by advertisements. Booking accommodation directly with the owner rather than through a comparison site can also save a surprising amount, particularly for longer stays.
quests.question: How can summer beach holidays become less economical?
options: Flight prices in peak months can cancel out the savings
Beach hotels are always more expensive than city ones
Walking equipment costs too much for most people
Planning takes longer than for a city break
quests.correctAnswer: Flight prices in peak months can cancel out the savings
quests.hint: The beach option's advantage is qualified by a "though" clause.
quests.explanation: Lower daily cost may be cancelled by expensive July and August flights. Planning is described as easier for beaches.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: From next month, we will require two-step verification for all customer accounts. After you enter your password, we will send a six-digit code to your phone by text message, which you must enter within five minutes. This adds a layer of protection: even if a criminal learns your password, they cannot log in without the code. Customers who do not have a mobile phone can choose to receive the code by an automated call to a landline, or use a small security device, which we will send free of charge. You will not be asked to enter a code each time; on devices you have registered, verification is required only once every thirty days. We will never ask you to tell us a code, and any message asking for one should be treated as fraud. Customers who lose their phone should contact us at once, and we will help them switch to an alternative method within a day.
quests.question: How often must a registered device be verified?
options: Once a year
Every five minutes
About once a month
On every login
quests.correctAnswer: About once a month
quests.hint: A condition, "on devices you have registered", changes how often codes are needed.
quests.explanation: For registered devices, verification is needed once every thirty days. The five minutes is how long the code stays valid.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: The old railway viaduct in Aldergate has been closed to trains since 1968 and has spent decades slowly decaying. Last spring, a charity raised funds to convert it into a raised walkway, with planting, benches and a small gallery at the midpoint. Engineers had to reinforce the arches and install drainage, and rare bats that roost in the stonework required a special licence and delayed the project by six months. The route, which is 1.2 kilometres long, opened to the public in June and attracted forty thousand visitors in the first month, far more than expected. Local cafes report higher trade, and some residents complain about litter and noise in the evening. The charity says it will introduce closing times and add extra bins. Guided tours, led by volunteers who once worked on the railway, are offered on Sundays and are free of charge.
quests.question: Why was the project delayed?
options: Engineers had to reinforce the gallery at the midpoint of the route
Visitors complained about noise from the new walkway
The charity ran out of funds before the work could begin
Protected bats living in the stonework needed special arrangements
quests.correctAnswer: Protected bats living in the stonework needed special arrangements
quests.hint: A delay is normally explained in a phrase mentioning what "required" extra time.
quests.explanation: Bats roosting in the stonework required a special licence, delaying the project by six months. Visitor complaints came after the opening.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Many people assume that expensive skincare products are more effective, but dermatologists say the price often reflects marketing rather than science. The key ingredients in most moisturisers, such as glycerine and petroleum jelly, are inexpensive and have been used for decades. Some costly creams contain genuinely useful compounds, like retinol, but in very small amounts, and the packaging may allow them to break down in light. A survey of products sold in pharmacies found that the cheapest performed as well as luxury brands in tests of hydration. Dermatologists therefore suggest choosing simple products without perfume, which is a common cause of irritation, and using sunscreen every day, which has the strongest evidence of preventing skin damage. The best routine, they say, is one you can keep up. Dermatologists also warn that products claiming to remove wrinkles overnight usually rely on temporary swelling of the skin.
quests.question: According to the passage, what has the strongest evidence of preventing skin damage?
options: Products sold in luxury packaging
Moisturisers with perfume
Expensive creams with retinol
Daily use of sunscreen
quests.correctAnswer: Daily use of sunscreen
quests.hint: The superlative in the second-to-last sentence points to the answer.
quests.explanation: Dermatologists mention sunscreen as the practice with the strongest evidence. Retinol may help but is present in tiny amounts.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: When the manager of the Riverside Cafe cut the lunch menu from thirty items to twelve, staff feared customers would complain. Instead, service became faster, food waste fell by half and, surprisingly, sales rose. The manager explains that with fewer choices, kitchen staff can prepare dishes more consistently and customers decide more quickly, which frees tables sooner. She also noticed that regulars tended to order the same five dishes anyway. The cafe now changes two items each month to keep the menu interesting, and it uses the same ingredients across several dishes so that fresh produce is used before it spoils. Not everyone approves: one longtime customer wrote to say that he misses the vegetable curry that was dropped. The manager replied with an invitation to suggest a new one. Sales of soup and sandwiches have risen most, and the cafe now plans to open on Sunday evenings as well.
quests.question: Why did sales rise after the menu was reduced?
options: The manager advertised more in local papers
Customers preferred the new vegetable curry
Faster service freed tables for more customers
The cafe increased its prices at lunchtime
quests.correctAnswer: Faster service freed tables for more customers
quests.hint: Follow the chain from fewer choices to quicker decisions.
quests.explanation: With fewer options, customers decide faster and tables free sooner, allowing more sales. Waste reduction is a separate benefit.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Under the university's new attendance policy, students who miss more than three sessions of a module without a valid reason may be asked to meet their tutor and could lose the right to sit the final exam. Valid reasons include illness supported by a note from a doctor, bereavement and religious observance. Students with long-term conditions should register with the support office, which can agree adjustments in advance, such as allowing recorded lectures instead of attendance. The policy does not apply to postgraduate students conducting research, who are managed by their supervisors. Lecturers will record attendance electronically using a card reader at the door. Students must tap their card on arrival, and tapping in for a friend is treated as a serious offence. Appeals against decisions can be made within ten days. Lecturers will also tell students in the first week which sessions are compulsory and which are optional.
quests.question: Who is NOT covered by the attendance policy?
options: Students who are ill
Students with long-term conditions
Students who tap in late
Postgraduate research students
quests.correctAnswer: Postgraduate research students
quests.hint: Look for the sentence containing a negative and a named group.
quests.explanation: Postgraduate researchers are managed by supervisors and excluded. Students with long-term conditions are covered but can agree adjustments.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: There is a simple experiment that demonstrates why the sky is blue. Shine a torch through a glass of water containing a few drops of milk. Seen from the side, the beam looks slightly blue, but the light that comes out of the far end of the glass is orange. The same thing happens in the atmosphere. Sunlight contains all colours, but tiny particles scatter blue light more than red, so blue reaches our eyes from every direction. At sunset, light travels through much more air, so most of the blue is scattered away before it reaches us, leaving the reds and oranges. This is why the sun looks orange near the horizon, and why a clean, clear sky appears deeper blue than a hazy one. Teachers often use this demonstration with children, because the materials are cheap and the change of colour is easy to see in a dark room.
quests.question: What is the purpose of the milk-and-torch experiment?
options: To measure the speed of light in a glass
To prove that milk is naturally a blue liquid
To demonstrate why sunsets feel colder than noon
To show on a small scale how air scatters light
quests.correctAnswer: To show on a small scale how air scatters light
quests.hint: Ask what the glass of water is a model of.
quests.explanation: The experiment mimics the atmosphere: the side view shows scattered blue and the far end shows the orange that remains.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: The Beaumont Prize for community projects is awarded annually to a group that has improved life in its neighbourhood. Applications must include a description of the project, evidence of its impact and a letter of support from at least one local organisation. Entries from schools, sports clubs and volunteer groups are welcome, but projects run by commercial companies are not eligible. The winning group receives $8,000 and a trophy, while two runners-up each receive $2,000. A panel of five judges, none of whom may have connections to the applicants, will draw up a shortlist and visit each finalist. Applications close on 30 April, and the winners will be announced at a ceremony in June. Groups that were unsuccessful may apply again in future years with the same project. Entries will be scored on creativity, how many people benefit and whether the project can continue without further funding.
quests.question: Which group would NOT be able to apply?
options: A school choir raising money for a trip
A company running a project to make a profit
A volunteer garden group in a local park
A sports club for teenagers in the town
quests.correctAnswer: A company running a project to make a profit
quests.hint: Read the sentence listing who is welcome, then the exception attached to it.
quests.explanation: Commercial companies are excluded, while schools, clubs and volunteers are welcome.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: A new supermarket has opened at the edge of town, and its effect on the high street is already visible. Two shops, a shoe repairer and a small greengrocer, have closed, and footfall in the market square has dropped by about a fifth. The supermarket points out that it has created seventy jobs and that its car park is free, which attracts shoppers who previously drove to the next town. Campaigners want the council to introduce free parking on the high street and to limit the size of future developments. The council has agreed to review parking charges but says it cannot stop a legal application that meets planning rules. Some traders believe that instead of competing on price, they should offer things the supermarket cannot, such as repairs, advice and local produce. A survey carried out by the local newspaper found that most residents still prefer to buy fresh bread and meat from independent shops.
quests.question: What do some traders think they should do?
options: Move their shops to the edge of town
Lower their prices to match the supermarket
Ask for the supermarket to be closed
Offer services that a supermarket cannot provide
quests.correctAnswer: Offer services that a supermarket cannot provide
quests.hint: A phrase of contrast introduces the traders' idea.
quests.explanation: Instead of competing on price, they would emphasise repairs, advice and local produce. Free parking is the campaigners' demand.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: In 1928, Alexander Fleming noticed that mould had grown on one of his dishes of bacteria, and that the bacteria near the mould had been destroyed. He named the substance penicillin, but he struggled to purify it and did not believe it would become a useful drug. It was more than a decade later that a team in Oxford, led by Howard Florey and Ernst Chain, found a way to produce it in large amounts. During the Second World War, the drug saved thousands of wounded soldiers, and Fleming, Florey and Chain shared a Nobel Prize in 1945. Fleming himself often stressed that the discovery owed as much to chance as to skill, while historians remind us that without the Oxford team, penicillin might have remained a laboratory curiosity. Early production was so limited that doctors reportedly recovered penicillin from patients' urine in order to use it again.
quests.question: What was the Oxford team's contribution?
options: They named the substance and studied it alone
They found a way to produce penicillin in quantity
They noticed the mould growing on the dish in 1928
They won the war with the help of the drug
quests.correctAnswer: They found a way to produce penicillin in quantity
quests.hint: Compare what Fleming did with what the team achieved a decade later.
quests.explanation: Fleming observed and named it, but the Oxford team made large-scale production possible, which turned it into a medicine.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: Please note the following changes to the swimming pool timetable from 1 May. Lane swimming will be available from 6:30 to 9:00 in the morning and 12:00 to 2:00 in the afternoon, with an additional evening session on Wednesdays until 9:00. The children's lessons that used to take place on Saturday mornings will move to Sunday afternoons because of a rise in demand for public sessions. The toddler pool will now open at 9:30 instead of 9:00 on weekdays, to allow time for cleaning. The sauna remains open every evening except Monday. The gym, which shares the reception area, is unaffected. Members who booked lessons on Saturdays will be contacted by phone, and refunds are available for anyone who cannot attend the new time. Anyone with an existing booking for the old time should contact reception before the end of April to confirm the change.
quests.question: Why were Saturday lessons moved?
options: The sauna was closed for repairs all week
The pool needed cleaning on Saturday mornings
More people wanted public swimming sessions
The gym required more space for classes
quests.correctAnswer: More people wanted public swimming sessions
quests.hint: The reason appears in the sentence describing the lessons.
quests.explanation: A rise in demand for public sessions is given as the reason. Cleaning explains the later toddler-pool start.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: In the last decade, a network of volunteers across the country has begun to record wild bird sightings using a phone app. Each entry includes the species, the number and the location, and the data is checked automatically for anything unlikely. Researchers say the result is a picture of bird populations that would have cost millions to gather by professionals. Already, the records have shown that several species are moving northward as winters become warmer, and that some garden birds are declining in areas where hedges have been removed. Critics point out that volunteers tend to observe in accessible places, such as parks and gardens, so remote areas are under-represented. To reduce this bias, the project now encourages people to record from unusual locations and asks experts to fill in the gaps. More than forty thousand people took part last year, and the annual count now covers over two million records.
quests.question: What limitation of the volunteer data is mentioned?
options: The data is never checked
Only professionals may submit records
Remote areas are under-represented
The app cannot identify species
quests.correctAnswer: Remote areas are under-represented
quests.hint: The limitation is raised by critics and followed by an attempt to correct it.
quests.explanation: Volunteers mainly record in accessible places, so remote areas are underrepresented. The project encourages sightings from unusual locations.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: A colleague's message can be read in many ways, and email hides tone. A short reply of "Fine." may be efficient to one reader and cold to another. Researchers who asked pairs of people to send sarcastic and serious messages found that senders were confident they had been understood, yet recipients guessed correctly only about half the time. Even close friends made the same mistake, though slightly less often than strangers. The lesson is not to avoid email but to compensate for what it lacks. Add a sentence that states your intention, such as "I'm happy with this," and use a call when a matter is delicate. Avoid sarcasm with people you do not know well. If a message upsets you, wait before replying, and consider whether the sender may have written it in a hurry. Most misunderstandings are accidents, not insults.
quests.question: What did the researchers' experiment show?
options: Sarcastic messages are usually meant to be cruel
Senders overestimated how well recipients understood their tone
Recipients always understood sarcasm correctly
Email is more reliable than telephone calls for tone
quests.correctAnswer: Senders overestimated how well recipients understood their tone
quests.hint: Compare how sure the senders were with how accurate the recipients were.
quests.explanation: Senders were confident they had been understood, but recipients guessed tone right only about half the time.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: The town council has published a summary of its plan for the seafront. The scheme has three phases. First, the crumbling promenade will be rebuilt with a wider path for cyclists and pedestrians, which is expected to cost six million dollars and be completed in two years. Second, the beach cafes will be replaced with a single building with a green roof and a public terrace, leased to an operator chosen by tender. Third, if the first two phases proceed on budget, the council will consider a small marina in the harbour. Consultation showed that residents strongly supported the path but were divided over the cafes, with a fifth worried about losing local businesses. The council says that existing traders will be invited to bid for the new lease. Copies of the full plan can be viewed at the library, and comments are welcome until the end of the month.
quests.question: On what condition will the marina be considered?
options: Residents vote in favour of it
The first two phases stay within budget
The promenade is completed in two years
Existing traders lose their leases
quests.correctAnswer: The first two phases stay within budget
quests.hint: Look at phase three for a conditional word.
quests.explanation: The marina will be considered if the first two phases proceed on budget. The two-year estimate concerns the first phase only.
